T09.reason: Codex is right that the page both asserts the DRAM's maker and says it is unknown. dram.capacity says '32 GB of LPDDR4X on these V3 cards (Micron part)'. The DRAM panel (memory-levels.script.js:5251, copied into circuitkit.js) says 'from Micron on the V3 cards'. The part inspector and ml:dram:dram.org.part presume 'the Micron part number'. Yet out.card.5 says 'Which maker's DRAM the lab cards carry is not recorded'. No verified finding covers this: dram-capacity-8-to-32, applied, kept '(Micron part)'. Checking Codex's proposed scope ('32 GiB LPDDR4X on the measured cards') against the lab's own records shows a larger error. The three measured cards do not all have 32 GB. The runtime's device-info dump, saved with every run, prints 'DRAM size (B): 34265366528' (32 GiB less 90 MiB) in every aifoundry2 and aifoundry3 log. It prints 17085497344 (16 GiB less 90 MiB) in every aifoundry1 card 1 log: 2,444 dumps over six campaigns, 25-29 Sep. The runtime takes this size from the driver (ETSOC1_IOCTL_GET_USER_DRAM_INFO, DevicePcie.cpp:350, 358), and it is the service processor's: BL2's ddr_config reads the DRAM's density register MR8 at boot and sets ddr_mem_size from it (code 4 = 16 GB, code 6 = 32 GB). The master minion passes it to the host less the region below HOST_MANAGED_DRAM_START (90 MiB). I ruled out the alternatives. BL2 0.18.0 (release 1.2.0, aifoundry1 card 1's firmware) has the same MR8 decoder. The hard-coded 16 GB is only in the fast-boot and test builds, which skip DRAM training entirely. The runtime's cap is 32 GB in both versions. So aifoundry1 card 1 has 16 GB, 1 GB (8 Gbit) per channel. The lab's notes never record this, and aifoundry1 card 0 has no record. On the maker: the vendor's document names its '32GB (Micron part) v3 card'. Its p. 2 photo shows four SK hynix H9HCNNNCRMBLPR-NEE packages, 32Gb (4GB) each by SK hynix's LPDDR list, so a 16 GB card. Its p. 8 photo shows Micron packages whose code is cut off at the photo's edge. The firmware supports Micron, SK hynix and Samsung and logs MR5 at boot, but no log is captured, so no lab card's maker is recorded. The fix scopes the capacity per card and states the maker as the vendor names it, in the chip fact, the memory levels' facts, the two DRAM panels, the memory levels' summary row and its ask. New numbers go through N rows, as the page does. out.card.5 is already right and stays. Generic mentions of 'the card's 32 GB' (the card blurb, out.card.3, ladder-outer.js:759, script.js:1163 and 2929) describe a 32 GB V3 card like aifoundry2's and can stay. The 131,072-row geometry is the controller's map: with ECC off the firmware always programs the map for the largest part (memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4638-4655), so it holds for the 32 GB cards. One note for the D-memlevels fixers of jedec-trfcab-16gb and dram-jedec-trfc-280: their '16 Gb per channel, JEDEC asks 380 ns' holds on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3. On aifoundry1 card 1, 8 Gb per channel, the programmed 280.7 ns meets JEDEC's 280 ns, so their new text should say 'on the 32 GB cards'.
